adjudication.evidence: Original N/E/U show a sustained offset beginning ~645 (E and U jump up, N down) and returning ~685 (E and U drop, N rises), forming a clear temporary platform. P1 starts too early (639) before the observed E/U jump; P3 is implausibly large (e.g., U +23.7 MAD) and inconsistent with smooth interior motion. P2 (645–685) aligns with both onset and return boundaries in all components and matches the numerically accepted interval (639–679 refined to 645–685 by observations). Interior points between 645–685 are stable after the initial jump, supporting a genuine temporary platform. Independent steps at 649 and 666 lie within but do not invalidate the platform.
